strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: active-triple-equalization-newton
Replacement scope: Replace the incumbent's active-set SLSQP loop and both Powell polishes (the block from "# --- active-set refinement loop" through the final "Powell polish") with a Gauss–Newton equalization solver operating in direct (u,v) barycentric coordinates per point (u_i, v_i with u,v ≥ 1e-7, u+v ≤ 1−1e-7), 22 free variables, no softmax.
Compute budget: at most 60 Gauss–Newton iterations, each solving a ≤(22+8) least-squares system (rank-revealing lstsq, cost microseconds); ≤10 active-set refreshes. Replaces ~40 s of SLSQP/Powell work; expected evaluation time drops to ~25–35 s.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's active-set SLSQP converges slowly on the epigraph form and the nonsmooth Powell polish barely moves. Each triangle area is exactly a quadratic (in fact bilinear-plus-quadratic) function of the (u,v) coordinates when the orientation sign is fixed, so signed areas s_j(P) have analytic gradients and Jacobians that are linear in P. The new degrees of freedom the incumbent lacks: (i) drop |·| by pinning each active triple's orientation sign from the incumbent (signs only flip through zero area, which never happens near the optimum), making the whole problem smooth; (ii) form residuals r_j = s_j − mean(s_active) over the triples within 5% of the minimum and solve one Gauss–Newton step with a trust region of 1e-2 in P-space, accepting only if the true min area over all 165 triples strictly improves; (iii) re-select the active set and repeat. This gives second-order convergence on exactly the quantity being scored, instead of first-order epigraph SLSQP followed by a derivative-free method that treats the problem as a black box. The current incumbent's active set is small (typically 3–8 triples from the tightest configuration), so the Jacobian is well-determined.
Plan: unpack best_B to (u,v) = (b_1, b_2) per point; compute signed areas with precomputed index arrays i0,i1,i2; loop: select active triples (area ≤ 1.05·min), build J (8-ish rows × 22 cols) with entries ∂s_j/∂(u_i,v_i) = analytic from the cross-product formula, solve min‖J d + r‖ with clip into the feasible box and trust radius, evaluate exact min over all 165, accept/reject, refresh active set; stop on no-improvement or active-set repetition. Feasibility is structural (box clipping with 1e-7 margin inside the 1e-6 evaluator tolerance); the best valid incumbent is kept on every rejected step.
Expected-gain check: the transformation is a strict solver upgrade on the exact scored quantity — if the active-set SLSQP incumbent is not already at a KKT point of the equalized system, one Newton step moves it, giving a falsifiable threshold of combined_score > 0.911747 on the evaluator whenever the final active-set residuals are not already zero (they are not, since Powell's typical step sizes leave 1e-6–1e-5 area slack).

strategies.title: [leave-one-out-reinsertion] Optimize a 10-point subproblem exactly, then reinser
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: leave-one-out-reinsertion
Replacement scope: Replace the pair-swap-descent block (section after the active-set loop, from `classify` through the final Powell polish) with a leave-one-out scheme; keep the seed enumeration, continuation, and active-set phases unchanged.
Compute budget: 11 outer rounds (one per removed point); each round: one 10-point softmin continuation (≤4 temperatures × 150 SLSQP iters) plus one dense 21×21 barycentric grid scan for reinsertion and one bounded SLSQP polish (≤200 iters). Expected eval time ≈ same order as current 110 s; cap total with a wall-clock guard at ~150 s, returning the incumbent on expiry.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's discrete moves (edge swaps, migrations) only reshuffle the *current* topology. Removing one point yields a 10-point max-min problem with C(10,3)=120 triples and far fewer active constraints, which the existing continuation+active-set machinery solves to a strictly higher per-triple minimum; reinserting the removed point into the *re-optimized* 10-point layout via a fine grid scan followed by local polish explores a genuinely different basin than polishing the frozen 11-point incumbent. Plan: (1) From the incumbent best_B, for each k in 0..10: delete point k, run the existing softmin continuation (t = 40, 400, 4000, 20000) on the remaining 10 points with the same softmax-barycentric parameterization (33 free variables), then the active-set epigraph polish. strategies.title: [symmetry-snap-relax] Snap near-C3 orbits to exact threefold symmetry, then re-r
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: symmetry-snap-relax
Replacement scope: Insert as a new phase immediately after the active-set refinement loop and before the pair-swap-descent block (which then runs on the new incumbent); the seed enumeration and first continuation are untouched.
Compute budget: One snap (pure numpy averaging, negligible cost) plus at most 3 re-anneal runs (refine with t = 40, 400, 4000, 20000, ≤200 SLSQP iters each) and one Powell polish (≤400 iters). Adds well under 30 s to the ~110 s baseline.
Gain mechanism: The optimizer's iterates drift off the exact C3 orbits the seed started on; small asymmetric residuals pin the active-set and swap heuristics to a slightly off-center basin. Averaging each near-orbit triple under the exact 120° barycentric rotation (component cycle [2,0,1]) and any near-fixed point to the centroid restores exact symmetry at negligible area cost, and the *unconstrained* re-anneal from this exactly-symmetric point can then slide along symmetry-preserving directions the noisy incumbent could not resolve — a basin re-centering the incumbent lacks. This is distinct from c3-orbit-reduction (which *constrained* the search to orbits and lost the free degrees of freedom); here symmetry is used only as a repair/warm-start, and the subsequent optimization is fully free.
Plan: (1) Classify incumbent points: a point is near-vertex-orbit if its smallest barycentric component exceeds 0.02; group points into candidate C3 orbits by checking whether the rotated set {B[k][[2,0,1]]} matches another point within barycentric tolerance 0.05, plus any point within 0.05 of (1/3,1/3,1/3) as a fixed point. (2) For each detected orbit of size 3, replace all three members by the orbit of their C3-average; for a detected near-centroid point, snap to exactly (1/3,1/3,1/3). (3) Verify the exact min area of the snapped configuration is within 5% of the incumbent's (else skip); run the existing `refine` continuation plus one active-set epigraph round from the snapped barycentric log-coordinates, fully unconstrained. (4) Accept only if the exact 165-triple minimum strictly improves; otherwise keep the incumbent. Softmax barycentric parameterization keeps all points strictly interior (feasibility margin ≫ 1e-6), and the `valid` distance check blocks duplicates. Expected-gain check: exact C3 symmetry removes the asymmetric drift that currently pins the active set, so the re-anneal can recover the symmetry-preserving improvement directions the incumbent's noisy iterate blocks — falsifiable threshold: min_area_normalized > 0.034347, with the known symmetric-seed family (three medians + centroid) indicating the snapped basin is nonempty and distinct.

strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: point-splitting-homotopy
Replacement scope: Add as an alternative seed-generation and warm-start phase feeding the existing `refine` continuation, replacing the reflected-image warm start (`refl(best_B)` run) and running before the active-set loop; all downstream phases operate on the best incumbent as before.
Compute budget: 10 splitting candidates (one per point of the best 10-point layout); each gets one continuation run (t = 20, 100, 500, 2500, 10000, ≤200 SLSQP iters per temperature) plus one bounded Powell polish (≤300 iters). Adds roughly 40–60 s; keep the existing wall-clock guard and drop remaining candidates on expiry.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent reaches n=11 only through 11-point seeds, whose local basins are shaped by the seed's topology. Starting from a well-optimized 10-point configuration (obtained by the existing pipeline applied to the 10 best of the 11 incumbent points, or by deleting the point whose removal maximizes the 10-point minimum — computable exactly from the incumbent in closed form) and splitting one point into two points offset by ±δ along the local gradient of the smallest area involving it gives a *continuation path in n*: the pair separates smoothly, and the homotopy lands in an 11-point basin that no 11-point-seeded local search can reach. The corrected bottleneck is the seed topology itself, not the optimizer.
Plan: (1) From the incumbent best_B, compute for each k the exact 120-triple minimum of the 10-point set with point k removed; take the best k*, giving layout B10. (2) Re-optimize B10 with one short continuation (t = 100, 1000, 10000) to sharpen it. (3) For each of the 10 points j of B10 (bounded budget: all 10), construct an 11-point seed by duplicating point j into two points at barycentric positions B10[j] ± δ·d, where d is the unit barycentric direction maximizing the smallest area involving j (found by a 24-direction barycentric circle scan at radius δ=0.01, evaluated exactly), renormalized to sum 1 with a 0.01 margin. (4) Run the existing `refine` continuation from each seed; the temperature schedule naturally anneals the pair apart as the softmin sharpens. (5) Keep the best exact-min valid result; incumbent fallback on any exception. Feasibility: all constructed points are strictly interior barycentric with margin ≥ 0.01, the `valid` check rejects coincident pairs if the split collapses, and the returned array is always the best valid incumbent. Expected-gain check: the split-pair homotopy exposes the one degree of freedom no incumbent phase has — a continuous deformation from the (strictly higher-minimum) 10-point optimum to an 11-point configuration — so it can land past the incumbent's basin; falsifiable threshold: min_area_normalized > 0.034347 on the evaluator.
